GoboLinux: A Linux Distribution With New Filesystem Hierarchy FOSS Post
This file system looks too much like the one Windows uses for my liking.

It is actually more like the one on a Mac (which is a genetic UNIX remember) although some of the names differ such as /Applications rather than /Programs. That said, I've had little trouble switching between MacOS and Linux although there are certainly some areas that they differ substantially such as /etc. The good thing about UNIX is you can do this and preserve backwards compatibility through symlinks.
Or alternatively, we could leave stuff alone that doesn't need fixing.

I don't disagree. I don't particularly like spaces in filenames and directories, and I also don't like mixing case since UNIX is case sensitive. Interestingly though, the HFS file system on a Mac isn't case sensitive so /Applications is the same as /applications as far as the shell is concerned but other parts of the file system are case sensitive such as the user's home directory. I generally treat it as being case sensitive and so prefer to use lower case all the time. Apple has walked a fine line between usability and integrating the underlying UNIX with the traditional Mac Finder. Mostly it works. Mostly.
